title: Implement the guided development governance session

requirement.summary: Continue the reviewed product plan by replacing repeated low-level task, context, base, check, and finish arguments with one confirmed govern start workflow and a safe working-copy-local active task pointer.

objective.rationale: A development-time governance product must make the governed path easier than manually composing its low-level contracts while preserving explicit human admission and authority boundaries.

goal: Add a previewable govern start flow that discovers or creates one compact admitted task, selects governance, records the comparison base, and lets govern check and finish safely resume that task.
non_goals: Do not add Git hooks, a daemon, IDE mutation, automatic commits, pushes, pull requests, merge, deployment, publishing, or release behavior.
Do not silently infer semantic scope, overwrite an existing task contract, or replace a different active task without explicit confirmation.
Do not turn the working-copy session pointer into a second source of truth for task or governance content.
Do not remove the existing low-level task, context, scope, evidence, or Monitor commands.
acceptance_signals: govern start can preview and explicitly confirm either one discovered admitted task or a newly scaffolded compact task with machine-checkable include paths and validation commands.
A strict untracked .agentgov/current-task.json stores only working-copy session facts and never silently replaces a different active task.
The start event records the selected governance references without claiming that a coding agent consumed them.
govern check and govern finish can default to the active task; finish also defaults to the recorded comparison base and runs fresh validation.
Task drift after start fails closed and instructs the user to restart governance instead of silently widening scope.
Dry-run and non-interactive execution do not write, and the complete repository suite passes.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_development_session tests.test_event_store tests.test_development_monitor tests.test_development_evidence -v

items: Automatic task discovery could select the wrong task when several admitted tasks exist.
A stale or tampered session pointer could make later commands govern the wrong scope.
A guided write workflow could imply authority that the human did not grant.

stop_conditions: Stop if start cannot disclose every target and require exact interactive confirmation before writing.
Stop if an existing task, tracked local-state file, symbolic link, Git index, source file, or branch would be overwritten or modified implicitly.
Stop if check or finish could proceed after the admitted task content changes without a new start.
Stop if automatic discovery needs semantic guessing or chooses among multiple eligible tasks.

decision.rationale: The user explicitly directed development to continue into the next productization phase after the local Govern, Observe, and Monitor loop was completed.
